Veronica isn’t your typical horror film; it’s a masterclass in psychological dread. Set in 1991 Madrid, it follows a young girl who holds a séance during a solar eclipse, unintentionally inviting a dark presence into her home. It’s widely considered one of the most haunting films ever made because it captures the raw, suffocating feeling of being hunted in your own living room. 

The director, Paco Plaza wanted the fear to feel as authentic as possible. In the movie, to achieve this, he didn't show the lead actress, Sandra Escacena, the "ghost" or the creature effects until the cameras were actually rolling. Her screams and reactions in these scenes aren't just acting they are genuine moments of shock and terror captured in real-time.

Fun Fact : This movie is based on the real "Vallecas Case," the real-life story of Estefanía Gutiérrez Lázaro. After she used a Ouija board, her house became the site of violent paranormal activity. It remains the only case in Spanish history where a police detective officially submitted a signed report stating he witnessed "unexplained and stressful" movements that couldn't be explained by science.
